title: Analysis of Solid Boron Injection for ITER
abstract: Since ITER will now operate with a full tungsten divertor and first wall, the ITER Organization is considering boron wall conditioning schemes to getter oxygen and reduce tungsten sputtering to avoid excessive radiation to ensure that ITER can reach and sustain high- performance plasma operation. ITER has adopted Glow Discharge Boronization (GDB) in deuterated diborane (B$_2$D$_6$) as its main technique, which can only be performed in the absence of magnetic fields, but has also requested a study to determine how effective solid boron injection (SBI), which can be performed during plasma operation, using either an Impurity Powder Dropper (IPD) or a boron pellet injector, might be as a risk mitigation to achieving Q=10. Solid impurity injection has been used for decades as a wall conditioning technique on numerous tokamaks and stellarators around the world. The study presented here begins to assess SBI on ITER by first quantifying the boron source term across a particle size scan from 1 $μ$m to 5 mm diameter and an injection velocity scan from 5 -- 200 m/s for several ITER plasma conditions: 1) Start of Research Operations (SRO) diverted L-mode, 2) Q=10 H-mode, and 3) low plasma current and low power limiter operation. Modeling of the ablation, transport, erosion and redeposition of solid boron is being carried out with the Dust Injection Simulator (DIS), the Neutral Gas Shielding (NGS), EMC3-EIRENE and WallDYN3D models. In the first steps presented here, the DIS and NGS models are compared for calculating the boron source term that is then used as input to EMC3-EIRENE and will later be used with WallDYN3D.
